sources.title: That Marvellous Murderbot
sources.author: Jumbled Thoughts of a Fake Geek Boy, 2025
sources.access_method: Identified Exit Strategy and Preservation status-quo paragraphs read
sources.read_scope: Basic support outside a subsistence-job requirement, internal exchange and external monetary trade.
sources.limitations: Review interpretation, not a complete economic charter. Calling the economy post-scarcity does not eliminate imports or useful jobs; the review is about the books.

sources.title: Murderbot and Story
sources.author: Jody Bower, 2024
sources.read_scope: Basic needs without charge and freedom to choose life activities.
sources.limitations: Qualitative critical account; no work census, equal-ownership proof or claim that every outsider receives identical rights.

sources.title: Why does the Corporation Rim exist?
sources.author: Murderbot Wiki community discussion, 2022

sources.read_scope: Recyclers make basic goods cheap and low-level bots provide services; participants debate the Rim’s scarcity.
sources.limitations: Fan interpretation of shared setting technology, not independently verified production statistics. Hypotheses about exotic matter and unavoidable forced labor are not adopted. A separate Preservation page was denied and not bypassed.

sources.title: Is this propaganda? Preservation in books and television

sources.read_scope: Readers dispute total post-scarcity and note book/television economic differences.
sources.limitations: Unverified discussion used as a limitation and continuity warning, not proof of a television constitution or of complete independence from trade.

sources.title: Perihelion
sources.author: Murderbot Wiki contributors
sources.access_method: Public indexed ship provision description read
sources.read_scope: ART provides food and recycled clothing and has a university association.
sources.limitations: One ship’s crew provisions do not establish the university society’s universal access. Ship AI agency is not the entire economy’s government.

sources.title: The Terraformers
sources.author: Publishers Weekly, 2022
sources.read_scope: Corporate ecological work, Spider City, public transport design and later housing crisis.
sources.limitations: Collective action and human/nonhuman personhood do not alone establish a labor-independent material economy. The review’s Sasky spelling is not used to overwrite the work’s Sask-E label.

sources.title: Indenture Rights for All: Challenging the Human Status Quo in Annalee Newitz’s Autonomous
sources.author: Springer Nature scholarly chapter, 2025
sources.access_method: Public indenture and compulsory-work passages read
sources.read_scope: Human and robot labor, transferable ownership and stimulant-driven work.
sources.limitations: Personhood and labor exploitation are established; they do not automatically mean human labor has ceased to govern distribution. No verbatim passages are reproduced.

sources.title: Why this AI engineer is using sci-fi to unpack tech’s biggest problems
sources.author: Steven Melendez, Fast Company, 2021
sources.access_method: Public biotech-lab and competitive-gig-work paragraphs read
sources.read_scope: Automation and enhancement coexist with pressure to earn income against AI competition.
sources.limitations: Technological competition is not by itself a completed post-work support system or a deliberate employment-preservation policy.

sources.title: Machinehood
sources.author: S. B. Divya
sources.access_method: Public labor-rights and gig-economy description read
sources.read_scope: A future labor-rights conflict involving humans and artificial intelligence.
sources.limitations: Author description does not establish a stable general support arrangement; real-world policy suggestions in interviews are not fictional institutions.

societies.name: The Murderbot Diaries (Preservation — book continuity)

scope.period: The functioning Preservation order around Exit Strategy and subsequent station life
scope.population: Human residents supported within Preservation’s internal economy
exclusions: Corporation Rim inhabitants assigned Preservation guarantees
Every visiting ship’s crew counted as a permanent resident
AI and construct citizens automatically counted as human nonworkers

societies.description:
Preservation separates basic support from the need to earn an ordinary subsistence wage. Critical accounts describe necessities supplied without charge, while internal exchange and monetary dealings with outsiders continue. Recyclers and servicing bots help make goods and services readily available. Together these support a provisional technologically assisted provision economy, rather than the stronger claim that all scarcity and all useful work have disappeared.

The control estimate favors meaningful resident agency and a community that lets people choose their activities. It remains broad because those freedoms do not by themselves prove equal ownership of every productive facility, and independent bot agency must also be respected. External income and imports qualify claims of total economic independence without canceling internal guarantees. People still conduct surveys, care for others, operate the station and do chosen jobs; no nonworking percentage follows from their support rights. This record uses the books. Reported changes in the television adaptation, including its explanation of external finance, are left outside the scope rather than silently combined with the novel economy.

guarantees.basis: Two critical accounts describe free necessities and support independent of accepting a subsistence job; external exchange remains possible.

control.basis: Resident choice and community provision support a positive provisional control estimate, but facility ownership and independent bot interests remain incompletely documented.

nonworking.basis: Useful professional, care and voluntary activity persists without a population participation count.

evidence.claim: Internal necessities do not require a subsistence job, while monetary external trade can continue.
evidence.locator: Preservation-needs paragraph and Exit Strategy status-quo discussion

evidence.claim: Shared recycler and bot technology provides a plausible material mechanism; the exact scale is not verified.

uncertainties: Admission is provisional and reference-led; the mechanism relies partly on fan interpretation of setting technology.
Free internal basics do not establish total post-scarcity, complete autarky or equal productive ownership.
Regime 1 remains an alternative if material control proves more concentrated.
Independent bot and construct citizens do not silently enlarge the human participation denominator.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

decisions.reason: Clear internal basic provision plus recycler/bot support permits a scoped provisional Preservation record.
The Rim’s exploitative labor system is clear, but human labor replacement sufficient for a post-work regime is not established.
decisions.analysis: Cheap goods and robot services coexist with necessary human/construct labor. Fan hypotheses about why indenture persists are not treated as verified job-preservation policy.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as a labor-control comparison; skip deeper reading.

decisions.reason: ART’s ship provision does not establish the university’s broader economic guarantees.
decisions.analysis: Food and clothing supplied to a working crew do not prove labor-independent access for a defined resident society beyond the vessel.

decisions.reason: Sask-E’s ecological management depends on real work by sentient persons, not an evidenced supported leisure population.
decisions.analysis: Bioengineering and planetary infrastructure are not automatically nonhuman labor outside the relevant person denominator. The corporate order’s inequality does not alone make it a zero variant.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as an ecological-labor and personhood comparison.

decisions.reason: Independent communities and transit collectives are identified, but their general labor-independent material access is unresolved.
decisions.analysis: Participation and resistance to housing exploitation do not supply a completed common-provision economy; sentient trains remain working persons.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reading rather than scoring an unspecified final utopia.

decisions.reason: Robot and human indenture describe an exploitative labor economy without a verified post-work provision mechanism.
decisions.analysis: Artificial persons can perform real work. Ownership rights, stimulant addiction and emancipation are distinct from technologically ending wage dependence.

decisions.reason: Machinehood’s enhanced humans compete for real gig income; a post-work support or deliberate job-preservation system is not established.
decisions.analysis: AI competition and tabletop biotech are substantial automation themes, but do not show a continuing labor-independent support arrangement. Author suggestions for real-world UBI are not fictional policy.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reading; preserve the transition theme without inventing economic guarantees.

review_notes: Seven fast decisions and one provisional book-only Preservation record. Its secondary/fan mechanism evidence and control uncertainty stay explicit.
No television institutions are combined with the books. The denied Preservation page was not bypassed.
ART crew provision is not a university-wide entitlement, and independent sentient trains or bioforms are not automatically idle machinery.
Real-world policy suggestions by authors are not enacted fictional institutions.
